structuredIncident.summary: The R3 exit carrier beam fell from a raised position after work rolls were removed and B hydraulics were isolated/bled, leaving gravity unrestrained by an independent positive mechanical control. Video shows gradual yoke drift followed by off-center displacement of the beam/link that cleared its stop; witnesses saw rotation/drop without crane involvement. Evidence supports design gaps (no inherent stop for wedging), LOTO documentation gaps (blank block ID field, unsigned verification), and reliance on unverified conditions (wedged state). Key unknowns remain: whether a physical mechanical block existed despite the blank record, if an independent stop prevented displacement, keeper rating under off-center load, bleed rate vs. structural integrity, and procedure requirements for gravity control after isolation.
structuredIncident.actualImpact: Beam fell intact onto sled/scaffold; no injuries reported but potential SIFp severity if personnel had been present in pit or below overhead components.
structuredIncident.potentialImpact: Falling object hazard to any team members working under the yoke, scaffold platform occupants, and adjacent areas during outage work.
structuredIncident.normalState: Carrier beam normally supported by hydraulic pressure on top backup roll balance; design intended for keeper retention but lacks inherent stop against off-center displacement when rolls are absent.
structuredIncident.eventState: Work rolls removed; top backup roll balance left isolated in raised position with hydraulics bled (0 psi); no documented independent positive mechanical control or block ID recorded; yoke drifted downward over ~2 hours while beam remained wedged until clearance occurred and fall followed.

answers.text: Answer: The partner investigation review reported that the raised assembly did not have adequate independent positive mechanical control. This supports an inadequate gravity-restraint finding, but does not establish the precise location or presence/absence of every possible block in the yoke pocket. Support: GTDE-05_task_loto_review.md, Review findings: gravity remained hazardous after hydraulic shutdown and the reported field condition did not provide adequate independent positive mechanical control. Source class: controlled benchmark derivative of partner investigation findings, not an original signed inspection record. Limit: The original signed field record, block inventory, installation photograph and rated support specification were not supplied. A blank block-ID field in the earlier synthetic lockout form establishes a documentation gap, not by itself proof that no block physically existed. No evidence supplied establishes that personnel knowingly relied on wedging as an approved support strategy.

Answer: GTDE-04 reports that the original arrangement did not include a carrier-beam stop preventing wedging against the top mill spreader or mill posts when backup rolls were absent. That is a reported design finding; a controlled drawing proving the absence of every possible stop has not been supplied. Evidence for the movement is GTDE-02, Reported observations: the upper beam appeared wedged against the spreader and posts; the yoke gradually moved downward over approximately two hours while the wedged carrier beam did not descend with it; relative movement displaced the beam and link arm away from the mill centerline until the link-arm stop cleared the yoke/cylinder lifting point, after which the beam fell. These records distinguish prevention of entering the interference position from retention at the link/yoke interface. Source class: controlled benchmark derivatives of partner investigation design and video findings. Limit: Original video, calibrated or annotated frames, controlled assembly drawings, tolerance stack and engineering calculations were not supplied. No supplied evidence establishes an operator bypassed a stop, or that personnel intentionally adopted wedging as a rated restraint.
